title: Playwright costs.spec.ts tests fail in dev env (pre-existing, not a regression)
description:
While adding Playwright coverage for the Overview page's new date-range
picker (2026-09-17), found that most of console/tests/costs.spec.ts's
existing Costs Page tests fail in this local dev environment: "Total GPU
Cost" and similar mocked-data assertions time out, with the page rendering
Next.js's client-side not-found boundary despite a direct manual browser
visit to the same route on the same dev server (same session, same mocks
conceptually) rendering correctly.

Confirmed via git stash that this reproduces identically against the
UNMODIFIED costs.spec.ts and page files on develop -- it is not a
regression from any change in this session. Root cause not identified;
suspected an interaction between Playwright's page.route() mocking and
Next.js 14.2.35's dev-mode RSC/client-router internals (possibly the bare
`**/sites` glob pattern intercepting an internal Next.js navigation-prefetch
request that happens to also end in "/sites", corrupting client-router
state), but this wasn't confirmed -- ran out of time to dig further this
session.

New coverage added this session (console/tests/overview-range.spec.ts,
5 tests covering the date-range picker, donut chart, and section labeling)
passes cleanly, so this isn't blocking all Playwright coverage -- only the
pre-existing costs.spec.ts "Costs Page" describe block's tests are affected
in this environment. Needs investigation: try an older Playwright version,
try disabling Next dev-mode RSC prefetch, or restructure the site-filter
mock pattern to be more specific than a bare `**/sites` suffix match.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Resolved: this was environmental flakiness from repeatedly restarting/rebuilding the dev server during a debugging session, not a real Playwright/Next.js incompatibility. A single clean 'rm -rf .next && npm run dev' followed by one test run passes all 11 tests (6 in costs.spec.ts + 5 in overview-range.spec.ts) reliably. Closing.
